note: Baseline for the kit files this oversight layer enforces. If a hash changes, the Rules tab goes red and every new ledger row carries the new short hash, so a rule edit can never masquerade as history. This is drift detection against a recorded anchor, not a cryptographic guarantee: anyone with write access to this disk could re-record. The anchor that is hard to quietly change is the one published in the git commit — state/integrity.json is committed, so the diff is the tamper alarm.
